newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon to keep tighter watch on mergers.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon to keep tighter watch on mergers.

text.p: The Pentagon said on Tuesday it will mount a tighter watch for potential damage from U.S. defence industry mergers on the future cost, quality and availability of military weapons.

Defence Undersecretary Paul Kaminski said he was taking steps recommended in a new study to avoid possible harm to small firms from such mega-mergers as Boeing Co.'s planned $14 billion acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp.

The Pentagon worries that mergers sparked by shrinking U.S. military budgets are creating industry giants that can build arms without buying parts and services from other firms, battering competition in the military-industrial base.

Kaminski released a study by the Defence Science Board Task Force on Vertical Integration and Supplier Decisions. It recommended, among other steps, better training of Pentagon anti-trust watchers and careful monitoring of key products and technology to identify future problems from mergers.
"I endorse the report and I have directed that the recommendations be implemented fully and immediately," Kaminski told reporters.

Federal regulators have not yet given any formal go-ahead to the planned merger of Boeing and McDonnell, a move which would create a firm with some 200,000 employes and annual sales of nearly $50 billion.

While the Defence Science Board report, which was commissioned by Kaminski, did not see major problems to date, it added that "we believe vertical integration poses potential future concerns to the Defence Department."

"All of the effects of these new industry conditions cannot yet be assessed, but they could promote new incentives for firms to leverage their vertical capabilities over time in ways that could be harmful to defence product cost, quality or performance," the report warned.
